title: Suncrest - Access and Data Lifecycle Orientation
summary: Introductory security posture intake focused on access controls, encryption key ownership, audit log retention and whether Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private fits Suncrest's compliance needs. Agreed to follow up with SOC2/ISO artifacts, architecture diagram for private VPC option, and schedule a deeper SE-led performance/PKI session.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
action_items: Avery to share SOC2 Type II and latest pen test summary
Nina to draft private deployment network diagram and KMS flow
Priya to send Suncrest compliance matrix (required controls + evidentiary artifacts)
Jordan to confirm expected retention windows for logs and input/output data
next_steps: Schedule SE-led deep dive on private deployment PKI and HSM (week of 2026-10-19)
Provide rough cost delta Hosted vs Dedicated for their projected QPS (by 2026-10-16)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-12
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 mins
Attendees: Avery (Redwood AE), Nina (Redwood SE), Jordan (Suncrest), Priya (Suncrest), Evan (Suncrest)

Summary note: conversation focused on gating items for security approval - access, keys, logs, retention, and where their apps should run.

[00:00] Avery (Redwood AE): Hey team, thanks for taking the time. Quick roll call?
[00:08] Jordan (Suncrest): Jordan here, Head of Infra.
[00:12] Priya (Suncrest): Priya, security.
[00:14] Evan (Suncrest): Evan, platform eng.
[00:18] Nina (Redwood SE): Nina here, I'll handle the technical bits.
[00:22] Avery: Great. We'll do quick intros, then go through your compliance checklist that Priya sent, and then talk hosting options.

[02:05] Priya: To set expectations, Suncrest needs SOC2 Type II and ISO 27001 alignment for anything that touches PII. Also SSO, SAML, SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapped to our internal roles — dev, infra, support. We want audit logs that we can push to our SIEM and retention for 12 months for logs, 7 years for transaction records.
[02:43] Nina: Got it. Two quick clarifying q's: when you say "transaction records" is that all prompt/response payloads or just the metadata?
[02:51] Priya: Ideally full request metadata and a hashed payload for anything PII; we need to be able to demonstrate data lifecycle. We can redaction on our side but need guarantees about retention windows and deletion APIs.

[05:10] Avery: On retention and deletion we offer configurable retention on Hosted and Dedicated — with Private you control everything. Hosted has default 30-day retention for text payloads unless you request stricter policies under an enterprise contract.
[05:27] Jordan: That 30-day default is a bit short for audit; can we extend to 90 or a year if needed?
[05:34] Avery: Yes, for enterprise customers we can negotiate retention SLAs and longer retention, but we need to discuss backup costs as that impacts pricing.

[07:50] Nina: Regarding SSO, Redwood supports SAML and OIDC and SCIM for user provisioning. For Dedicated we have an option to tie into your IdP via SAML with JIT provisioning and group-backed RBAC. For Private/VPC you can run the control plane behind your SSO too.
[08:20] Evan: How mature is the SCIM implementation? We use groups heavily and need group-sync to map to product roles.
[08:29] Nina: SCIM provisioning covers groups and user attributes, but we sometimes see mapping edge cases — e.g., role names with slashes — we'll send our mapping doc.

[10:05] Priya: KMS— we need customer-managed keys. Our security policy requires that keys are under our KMS and HSM where possible; we do not want Redwood having plaintext key escrow for certain data.
[10:20] Avery: We support BYOK on Dedicated and Private. Hosted can support envelope encryption where you hold the master KMS keys in your cloud account (Bring-Your-Own-Key) via our customer key integration, so Redwood never has access to decrypted master keys. There are a few technical caveats around cache and ephemeral tokens.
[10:45] Nina: To add, we can integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault; for HSM-backed keys we have a SRV layer that talks to your HSM via our private connector when on Private.
[11:12] Evan: When you say 'talks to your HSM', do you mean the runtime calls the HSM on every token gen or you cache derived keys?
[11:20] Nina: We do derived key caching for performance — the K-V cache is used to avoid per-token HSM roundtrips. But customers can opt for stricter mode that avoids local key caching at cost of latency. We'll document latency tradeoffs.

[13:32] Jordan: Audit logs — what formats and retention options do you provide? We need logs to ship to Splunk and also an immutable tamper-evident copy.
[13:45] Avery: We emit detailed audit logs (API calls, user actions, admin actions). For Hosted we stream logs to customer destinations via secure forwarding (TLS) or you can pull them via API. For Dedicated/Private you can host the log collector in your VPC and we can write directly to your S3 bucket or syslog endpoint.
[14:10] Priya: Tamper-evident — do you support append-only storage or signed logs?
[14:16] Nina: We have a signed log option for enterprise customers where logs are signed server-side; for Private it's simpler since you control storage and can enable immutability flags on the bucket.

[16:00] Priya: On certification — can you share SOC2 Type II report and scope?
[16:06] Avery: Yes, we'll share our SOC2 Type II report and our ISO alignment summary. Note some Hosted subsystems are shared multitenant components — we'll highlight the scope and compensating controls.
[16:28] Priya: We'll need the control matrix mapping to our internal controls — who owns evidence, where you store logs, retention, encrypt-at-rest and in-transit proof.
[16:40] Avery: We'll include a mapping document and a redaction checklist so you can see evidence types.

[18:55] Evan: Network isolation — can Dedicated be single-tenant in a VPC peered with our account? We want private network paths and no public endpoints for inference traffic.
[19:05] Nina: Dedicated has an option for VPC peering and private endpoints; Private gives you the control plane in your VPC so nothing traverses public network. There are implications for autoscaling and patching windows, we can explain those in the architecture doc.

[21:40] Jordan: How does patching and maintenance work for private? We have a strict maintenance window and change approval process.
[21:48] Avery: For Private we ship an operator bundle and coordinate patch windows; we also can do managed Private where Redwood schedules and executes patching under your change control. We'll outline SLAs.

[24:10] Priya: RBAC — can you tie resource-level permissions down to model, route, and environment? We need to restrict dev from production models and only a few users with admin audit access.
[24:24] Nina: Yes, our RBAC supports policy scoping by model, route, and environment. We also support role templates and attribute-based rules that can integrate with your IdP groups. Occasionally we see customers want attribute-based access that needs custom sync rules; we can support that via our SCIM mapping and API.

[26:55] Evan: Anything else around data residency? Some of our customers in EU require processing to remain in the EU.
[27:02] Avery: We have region pinning for Hosted and Dedicated — you can route inference to EU regions. For Private you choose the deployment region. For EU-only processing we'll need to confirm which models are available in each region because of licensing/weights distribution.

[29:40] Jordan: Are there any known limitations re: model variants and private deployments? Like quantized vs full fp16?
[29:48] Nina: For Private we support a subset of our catalog at GA; certain bleeding-edge quantized kernels require runtime updates. We'll provide a compatibility matrix. For Dedicated we maintain more variants but there can be lead times for new kernels.

[31:10] Priya: DLP and redaction — can Redwood provide pre-ingest redaction or do we have to handle that client-side?
[31:20] Nina: We recommend pre-ingest redaction in your pipeline, but we also offer a middleware hook in Dedicated and Private to perform redaction or tokenization before persistence. Hosted has a redaction pipeline for enterprise customers but with throughput caveats.

[33:55] Jordan: Cost tradeoffs — we need a rough sense of cost and how KMS/HSM usage affects it.
[34:05] Avery: Cost buckets: compute (model runtime), storage (retention), and network. Using customer-managed keys adds some operational costs (HSM calls, key rotation auditing) and can affect latency if you disable caching. We will produce a ballpark deck for your QPS and retention assumptions.

[36:30] Priya: One last governance point — we need an SLA that includes notification within 4 hours for security incidents and monthly attestation reports. Are those possible?
[36:42] Avery: We offer incident notification SLAs for enterprise contracts, and we can include monthly attestation or a quarterly security summary as an add-on. We'll capture this in the proposal.

[38:55] Nina: Quick note about evidence — we can provide logs, config snapshots, and signed timestamps for actions. For some items (like pen-test reports) we may provide executive summaries unless an NDA is in place.

[40:12] Evan: For the private deployment, what's the onboarding timeline? We have a pilot target in December.
[40:20] Avery: Pilot timeline: 4-6 weeks for Private (operator install, connectivity, initial model onboarding) if you have infra ready; Dedicated generally 2-4 weeks. We'll validate calendar and dependencies.

[42:00] Priya: We'll need to review the SOC2 and the private architect doc with our legal and infra next week.
[42:10] Jordan: Can you also include MOU language for data residency and key ownership?
[42:16] Avery: Yes, legal can draft MOU language; we'll start with standard template and highlight key clauses.

[44:05] Avery: Recap of next steps: we'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, private deployment diagram, SCIM mapping doc, and a rough cost delta. We'll get a calendar invite out for the SE deep dive next week.
[44:20] Priya: Sounds good. Thanks.
[44:25] Jordan: Thanks everyone.
[44:30] Evan: Thanks.
[44:35] Nina: Bye.

End of transcript.
notes: Redwood to mark Hosted components that are in-scope for SOC2 in the artifact package
Customer prefers BYOK and HSM-backed master keys for production
